metadata.title: Round 2 SME Review Packet
metadata.sub_family: Learning & Development Strategy and Design  +  Training Delivery
metadata.subtitle: Combined Round 2 focus group · the two specializations that share the Learning Design competency
metadata.specialization_label: Learning & Development Strategy and Design  +  Training Delivery
metadata.time_required: About 35 minutes for this focus group

how_this_works.what_we_did: We combined your Round 1 edits on the shared Learning Design competency into one proposed version, kept as many requested changes as possible, and expanded the definition to name needs-analysis, consulting, and facilitation alongside design. The expanded definition is already applied (Part A). The one item that genuinely needs the two specializations together, the design-versus-delivery boundary, is drafted as a recommendation (Part B).
how_this_works.what_we_need: Confirm the applied definition change in Part A. In Part B, settle which Learning Design indicators are designer-owned (Learning & Development Strategy and Design) versus delivery or product-owner scope (Training Delivery), and confirm how the sub-family carries Workforce Planning. Nothing in Part B is final until you decide.
how_this_works.where_feedback_went: Every Round 1 comment on these competencies is in the appendix disposition, including the Training Delivery edits (Tessa Sprengers, Tori Hulse) on role-blending, the technology indicator, and facilitator coordination.
how_this_works.status_intro: Every competency below carries a status label so you can see, at a glance, what is already settled and what still needs the group. Items are grouped into two parts: Part A holds changes we have already applied (read and confirm); Part B holds the items for live discussion (decisions and proposals).

ground_rules.text: Decide who owns each indicator and at what level, and for which specialization, before debating wording. Wording fixes already handled in the edit lane do not need this room.

At intake the hiring manager selects three to five competencies for the job. Set each competency essential, important, or limited per specialization; the job then selects its own set within the recommended size.
Owners and dates recorded at sign-off feed the decision registry; the sub-family owner is Vidula.

coverage.note: This matrix shows the complete union of competencies touched by both specializations (the L&D Strategy & Design Round 1 set of 5 and the Training Delivery set of 4). Learning Design & Strategy is shared and is the live item: Decision 1 settles which indicators are designer-owned (L&D Strategy and Design) versus delivery or product-owner scope (Training Delivery). Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy is carried by L&D Strategy and Design as a user or contributor, not an owner (Decision 2); it is not in the Training Delivery set. Talent Review & Succession Management, HR Service Delivery Excellence, and Workforce Analytics & HR Insights are carried or used by the sub-family at contributor and reporting levels; they were settled in Round 1 and are included here for completeness — read them in the appendix; only Learning Design and Workforce Planning need the group this session.

items.title: Learning Design & Strategy: scope and the design-versus-delivery boundary
items.owners_line: Learning & Development Strategy and Design, Training Delivery   |   15 min

rows: The definition seems focused on the Design and Development capability of L&D, and not consulting (needs analysis) or facilitation.

I don't disagree, but they're blending roles. Some of these things Designers would own, and others Product Owners would own. And: coordination of facilitators and evaluation is not something you typically see in this role.

Targeted workforce skills and capabilities are too vague (link to current and future business needs). Technology: the skill is leveraging available technology, not performing the build. Add at L4: continuous improvement and external L&D trends.

items.recommendation: Expand the competency to name needs-analysis and consulting and facilitation alongside design, with a clearer link to current and future business needs (the expanded definition is in the appendix). Resolve the role-blending: decide which indicators stay in Learning Design as designer-owned, and which move to delivery or product-owner scope (facilitator coordination and evaluation are the contested ones). Reframe the technology indicator as leveraging available technology, and add the L4 continuous-improvement and external-trends behavior.

decide.text: Adopt the expanded scope? Which indicators stay as designer-owned versus move to delivery or product-owner scope?

items.status_note: bring your view to the focus group
items.assigned_to: Learning & Development Strategy and Design · Training Delivery (as users or contributors)
items.title: Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy: ownership and level for this sub-family
items.owners_line: Learning & Development Strategy and Design, Training Delivery   |   10 min

rows: Until an owner is identified for Operational WFP and movement is made in the SWP space (we only have a definition today and it is not on the priority list). The competency reads as un-owned.
Establishing enterprise workforce-planning standards should be in strategic alignment with Cargill overall; the sub-family is a user, not the build owner.

items.recommendation: Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy stays a shared competency, but the Talent & Development sub-family is a user or contributor, not the owner. Operational workforce planning has no named owner and only a definition today, so do not place build-level expectations on these roles. Set the sub-family at use-output or support levels, and add the strategic-alignment-with-Cargill language Talent Advisory flagged. Operational workforce-planning ownership is routed to governance.

decide.text: Confirm the sub-family carries Workforce Planning at use or support levels, not owner, and that operational ownership is deferred to governance?

rows: Learning design ownership versus Talent Acquisition

Early Careers reviewers: Learning design is a component of a successful early career strategy, however, this work has clearly been owned by Talent Development, not TA. We do not expect our EC team to create these programs.
Owner-aligned: learning design sits with this sub-family, not Talent Acquisition. Early Careers teams ensure the business considers development needs but do not build programs.

disposition_register.intro: Every Round 1 comment on the competencies this pairing shares, grouped by competency, with how it was used. Nothing was dropped on a statistic.

entries.round1: Reviewers said the definition focused on design and development, not consulting or facilitation; Training Delivery (Tessa Sprengers, Tori Hulse) flagged role-blending between designers and product owners, said facilitator coordination and evaluation are not typical of the role, called the technology indicator a build rather than leverage, and asked to add an L4 continuous-improvement and external-trends behavior.
entries.outcome: Definition expanded to name needs-analysis, consulting, and facilitation (applied, Part A). The designer-owned versus delivery indicator split, the technology reframe, and the L4 addition are open as Decision 1.

entries.round1: Reviewers said the competency reads as un-owned (only a definition today, not on the priority list) and that establishing enterprise standards should align with Cargill overall; the sub-family is a user, not the build owner. Early Careers added that learning design sits with Talent Development, not Talent Acquisition.
entries.outcome: Kept as a shared competency carried by the sub-family at use or support levels, not owner; operational workforce-planning ownership routed to governance; strategic-alignment language added (Decision 2).

entries.round1: Carried in the L&D Strategy and Design and Training Delivery Round 1 sets; reviewed and rated, with no wording change requested. Owned by Performance & Talent Management and Talent Advisory.
entries.outcome: Carried by the sub-family as a contributor, not an owner; settled in Round 1 with no edits. Included for completeness; full indicators in Appendix B.

entries.round1: In the Training Delivery Round 1 set; reviewed and rated, with no wording change requested. It is the HR operations spine, owned by HR Operations.
entries.outcome: Carried at use levels by the sub-family; settled in Round 1 with no edits. Included for completeness.

entries.round1: In both the L&D Strategy and Design and Training Delivery Round 1 sets; reviewed and rated as a user-level competency, with no wording change requested by this sub-family.
entries.outcome: Used at a learning-reporting level (completion, transfer, evaluation data), not built; settled in Round 1. Included for completeness.

appendix.intro: Current indicators for the competencies in play, with accepted Round 1 edits applied. Read these as reminders before the session. The session decides ownership and level, not the wording. Every Round 1 comment is accounted for in Appendix A.
